awino.endpoint.description: OpenAI-compatible base URL or Anthropic base URL. Empty = provider default.

awino.mcpServers.description: MCP servers the sidecar spawns over stdio. Each: {name, command, args?, env?}. Their tools enter the harness registry under the same contract and approval gates. Note: env values are stored as plaintext workspace settings — never put secrets there; provider API keys belong in VS Code SecretStorage (Awino: Set Provider Key).

awino.provider.description: Model source for the harness. API keys are NOT stored here — use 'Awino: Set API Key'.

awino.bedrockRegion.description: AWS region for the Bedrock provider. The OpenAI-compatible endpoint is derived from it (https://bedrock-runtime.{region}.amazonaws.com/openai/v1); awino.endpoint overrides it when set.

awino.bedrockAuthMode.description: How the Bedrock provider authenticates: "api-key" uses the Bedrock API key from SecretStorage (Bearer); "aws-profile" signs every request with AWS SigV4 from the named awino.bedrockAwsProfile via the standard AWS credential chain (env, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.aws/config incl. source_profile, SSO cache). No key is needed or sent in aws-profile mode.

awino.bedrockAwsProfile.description: AWS profile name for Bedrock in "aws-profile" auth mode (see awino.bedrockAuthMode). Resolved from ~/.aws/credentials and ~/.aws/config; for SSO profiles run `aws sso login --profile <name>` first. Ignored unless bedrockAuthMode is "aws-profile".

awino.pythonPath.description: Python interpreter used to launch the Awino sidecar.

awino.keyLabels.description: Friendly labels for your API keys, e.g. {"openai": "Work"}. Labels are NOT secret — they are shown in the Models & Providers panel next to the key indicators. The keys themselves stay in VS Code SecretStorage and never appear here.

openai.description: Label for the OpenAI-compatible API key.

anthropic.description: Label for the Anthropic API key.

bedrock.description: Label for the Bedrock API key.

awino.script.description: TEST ONLY: scripted candidate turns for the scripted provider (set awino.provider to "scripted"). Each turn goes through the identical validation/judge/approval pipeline — it only feeds candidate turns instead of calling a model. Leave empty in normal use.
